fields.label: Setup Guide
fields.options:
How to set up Microsoft Teams (step by step)

You need a Microsoft 365 Global Administrator. Takes about 20 minutes.

  1. Register an app. Open Microsoft Entra admin center → App registrations → New registration. Name it "Meeting Sync", choose "Accounts in this organizational directory only", click Register.
  2. Copy the IDs. On the app's Overview page copy Directory (tenant) ID into Tenant ID and Application (client) ID into Client ID below.
  3. Create the secret. Go to Certificates & secrets → New client secret (24 months) → copy the Value (not the Secret ID) into Client Secret. It is shown only once. Set a reminder to renew it before it expires.
  4. Add permissions. Go to API permissions → Add a permission → Microsoft Graph → Application permissions, and add:
    CallRecords.Read.All, OnlineMeetings.ReadWrite.All, OnlineMeetingTranscript.Read.All, Calendars.ReadBasic.All, User.Read.All
    Then click Grant admin consent.
  5. Allow the app to read meetings. Teams needs an application access policy. A Teams admin runs this once in PowerShell (Microsoft guide), replacing the app ID with your Client ID:
    Install-Module MicrosoftTeams; Connect-MicrosoftTeams
    New-CsApplicationAccessPolicy -Identity "MeetingSync" -AppIds "<Client ID>" -Description "Meeting Sync"
    Grant-CsApplicationAccessPolicy -PolicyName "MeetingSync" -Global
    It can take up to 30 minutes to apply.
  6. Webhook Secret: type any long random text (for example 32 letters and numbers).
  7. Base URL: this site's public https address. Microsoft must be able to reach it from the internet.
  8. Tick Enable Microsoft Teams and save. Then use Actions → Renew Teams Subscriptions, and check the Error Log for any "[SUBSCRIPTION]" error.
  9. Test: hold a Teams meeting of 3 minutes or more with Record and transcribe on. A Meeting Call Log and a draft Meeting appear here within about 30 minutes after it ends.

fields.label: Setup Guide
fields.options:
How to set up Google Meet (step by step)

You need a Google Workspace super admin. Meet transcripts need Business Standard or higher (which plans). Takes about 20 minutes.

  1. Create a project. Open Google Cloud → New project, signed in as the Workspace admin. Name it "Meeting Sync".
  2. Enable 3 APIs in that project (click each link, then Enable): Google Meet REST API, Google Calendar API, Admin SDK API.
  3. Create a service account. Open Service accounts → Create service account, name it "meeting-sync", skip the optional roles, Done.
  4. Download the key. Open the service account → Keys → Add key → Create new key → JSON. Upload this file in Service Account Key below and tick Private while uploading. Do not share it by email or chat.
  5. Copy the Client ID. On the service account's Details tab copy the Unique ID (a long number).
  6. Give access in Workspace. Open Admin console → Domain-wide delegation → Add new. Paste the Unique ID as Client ID and paste these scopes (comma separated):
    https://www.googleapis.com/auth/meetings.space.readonly,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events.readonly,https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.user.readonly
    Only if you tick "Turn On Transcription Automatically", also add https://www.googleapis.com/auth/meetings.space.settings
  7. Workspace Admin Email: enter the admin's email address below.
  8. Tick Enable Google Meet and save. Then click Actions → Test Google Connection. Meet, Calendar and Directory should all show "ok": true.
  9. Test: hold a Google Meet call of 3 minutes or more and turn on Transcripts (Activities → Transcripts). Within about 30 minutes after it ends, a Meeting Call Log and a draft Meeting appear here. To check sooner, use Actions → Sync Google Meet Now.

Employees are matched by email, so each employee's company email in ERPNext must match their Google account.
